passed.title: Series.to_dummies adds a null indicator column unless drop_nulls=True
passed.trap: If the Series contains nulls, `Series.to_dummies` creates an extra indicator column for the null values by default. A model matrix built this way gets an unexpected feature column. Pass `drop_nulls=True` to skip that column, so null rows become all-zero vectors. `drop_first=True` drops the first category, not the null column. The indicator columns are `UInt8`, not boolean.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

s = pl.Series("a", [1, 2, None, 3])

default = s.to_dummies()
print(default.columns)

clean = s.to_dummies(drop_nulls=True)
print(clean.columns)
print(clean.dtypes)
print(clean.row(2))

passed.title: Series.upper_bound returns the dtype's limit, not the data maximum
passed.trap: `Series.upper_bound` ignores the values in the Series. It returns the largest value representable by the Series' dtype as a one-element Series. For example, it gives 127 for `Int8` and `inf` for `Float64`, not the largest finite float. Use `Series.max` for the largest value actually present. When you use `Series.upper_bound` as a sentinel, remember that it is infinite for float dtypes.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

s_int = pl.Series("s", [-1, 0, 1], dtype=pl.Int8)
print(s_int.max(), s_int.upper_bound().item())

s_float = pl.Series("s", [1.0, 2.5, 3.0], dtype=pl.Float64)
print(s_float.max(), s_float.upper_bound().item())
